summary: Describes a URN namespace that OASIS uses to name persistent resources it publishes, such as OASIS standards, DTDs, schemas, and stylesheets.

plainLanguage.summary: It gives each document an organization publishes a permanent name, like a library call number.

questions: what is the oasis urn namespace
how does oasis name its documents
subtitle: A namespace for OASIS to identify its published resources persistently.

tldr.problem: OASIS publishes many documents and resources (standards, schemas, stylesheets) that need unique, permanent, location-independent names that do not depend on where they are stored.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3121 defines a URN namespace called 'oasis' that OASIS organizations use to assign stable names to their resources following a hierarchical structure with branches for specifications, technical committee work products, and legacy documents.
tldr.outcome: OASIS and other organizations can now give their published resources persistent identifiers that survive relocation, allowing tools and documents to reference them reliably without worrying about broken links.

today: RFC 3121 is an Informational RFC that has not been obsoleted. OASIS continues to use the 'oasis' URN namespace defined in this document to assign persistent identifiers to its published standards, technical resolutions, and other resources.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
OASIS, the Organization for the Advancement of Structured Information Standards, publishes many types of documents: XML standards, stylesheets, schemas, and other technical resources. These documents need to be referenced reliably, especially because XML-based standards require all resources to have a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI).

The challenge is creating names that stay the same forever, regardless of where a document is stored on the internet. RFC 3121 solves this by defining a URN namespace (Uniform Resource Name) that OASIS can use to assign permanent names to all resources it publishes.
sections.plainLanguage: When your school gives you a student ID number, it stays the same even if you move classrooms. This RFC creates the rulebook for how OASIS assigns permanent ID numbers to its documents.

sections.title: The OASIS URN Structure
sections.content:
The OASIS URN namespace is named 'oasis' and has two main branches: names for published resources and member for member-assigned namespaces.

Under the names branch, there are three categories. The specification category is for OASIS standards and their associated documents like schemas and stylesheets. The tc (technical committee) category covers work products from OASIS committees. The technical category covers legacy documents such as technical notes, resolutions, and memoranda.

Each category has its own hierarchical structure. For example, a specification URN looks like: urn:oasis:names:specification:{specification-id}:{type}{:subtype}?:{document-id}. This structure lets OASIS assign unique identifiers to specifications, define the document type (such as a DTD or schema), and give each document a unique ID.
sections.plainLanguage: Think of it like a file cabinet with drawers labeled 'Specifications', 'Committee Work', and 'Old Documents'. Each drawer is organized by number so you can find any paper instantly, and the system never changes.

sections.title: Three Hierarchies for Different Resource Types
sections.content:
The specification hierarchy names OASIS standards and their components, with fields for the specification ID, document type (such as document, schema, stylesheet, entity, or xmlns), an optional subtype, and the document ID. The Director of Technical Operations at OASIS assigns all identifiers.

The technical committee hierarchy works similarly but is rooted at the committee level rather than the specification level, allowing committees to publish their own work products.

The technical (legacy) hierarchy covers older documents like technical notes and research papers, with a structure based on document type, year, and amendment ID. This preserves identifiers from OASIS's earlier systems.

The member hierarchy allows OASIS members to have their own sub-namespaces. Each member gets a unique member ID, and the string after that is opaque (meaning members can structure it however they want).
sections.plainLanguage: Different kinds of documents (new standards, committee work, old documents, and member stuff) each get their own filing system. This way OASIS can handle anything they publish without conflicts.

sections.title: Persistence and Resolution
sections.content:
OASIS commits to maintaining the accessibility and persistence of all resources assigned URNs. Once a resource is given a URN, that name will never change, even if the resource is moved or updated.

When someone needs to find a resource by its URN, OASIS distributes catalogs (based on OASIS TR9401 Catalogs) that map URNs to actual URLs where the resources can be retrieved. A more interactive online resolution system may also be deployed. This separation of the stable name from the current location is the key strength of URNs.

Assignment of identifiers is limited to OASIS and those it explicitly authorizes. OASIS will assign portions of its namespace to member organizations so they can manage their own sub-namespaces without needing OASIS to approve every name.
sections.plainLanguage: OASIS promises never to change a document's permanent name. When you look up a name, OASIS tells you where the document is today. If they move it tomorrow, the name stays the same, but OASIS updates where it points.
